structured_output.summary: The Ticket-consumption verification query in `consume` fails to bind Grant retention (shared Work vs dedicated Probe) to the invocation's role, unlike the sibling lease-lookup queries which correctly do so.
findings: In `consume`, the validation query's lease-ownership clause is `(l.invocation_id IS NULL OR l.invocation_id=i.id)` with no role-based branching. This accepts a match for ANY role as long as either condition holds, instead of enforcing that primary/postcondition invocations must use a shared Work Grant (`l.invocation_id IS NULL`) and probes must use their own dedicated Grant (`l.invocation_id=i.id`). Compare with `attached_launch_identity` and `request_attached_ticket`, both of which correctly gate on `role_text(job.role)` via `((?3='probe' AND l.invocation_id=?4) OR (?3!='probe' AND l.invocation_id IS NULL))`. The `consume` query omits the `?3='probe'`/`?3!='probe'` role discriminant entirely, so it would spuriously accept a probe invocation being satisfied by a shared Work Grant (invocation_id NULL, e.g. a Grant retained from an in-progress primary/postcondition sequence on the same allocation_key) or a primary/postcondition invocation being satisfied by a Grant scoped to a different, specific invocation_id — weakening the one-Grant-per-probe / shared-Grant-for-work-sequence invariant at exactly the point (Ticket consume) meant to be the final authorization check before commit.

Secondary/lower-confidence concern: `validate_next`'s Postcondition→Postcondition transition (with prior cleanup released) requires `last.role_index.checked_add(1) == Some(intent.role_index)`, i.e. strictly sequential, gap-free postcondition indices. If specification indices for postconditions are not guaranteed contiguous from zero (only stated to be 'their specification index'), a legitimate next postcondition whose spec index skips a value would be wrongly rejected as a role/order conflict. This is not as strongly corroborated as the first finding and should be checked against the postcondition indexing spec.
